transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Nova Head of ML), Sophie Chen (Infra Lead), Amir Patel (PM)

Summary (auto): walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profile recommendations, sample benchmarks comparing INT8 and FP8 on 7B/13B models, and pilot planning.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, uh on this call with Priya who'll do the deep dive on quantization and Optimize.
00:12 Marco Ruiz: Hi Jordan, hey Priya. Thanks, we pulled Sophie and Amir in. We're mainly trying to understand whether INT8 is good enough for our user-facing completion calls or we need FP8 for quality.
00:25 Priya Shah: great, thanks Marco. Quick agenda: a) quick primer on INT8 vs FP8 and where Redwood Optimize recommends each, b) sample benchmarks on latency and quality, c) how to run pilot on Dedicated, and d) next steps. Sound ok?
00:40 Marco Ruiz: yep, perfect.
00:46 Priya Shah: ok so quick background — INT8 is quantize-then-run, it's super cheap and lower memory, gives you big throughput wins, but depending on model and prompt distribution you might see quality regressions on edge cases. FP8 is a newer low-precision float that keeps more dynamic range so quality often closer to FP16 with smaller latency hit than full fp16.
01:10 Sophie Chen: quick q, when you say latency hit — are we talking token latency or end-to-end? Our main concern is 95th pct token latency for interactive chat.
01:18 Priya Shah: good call, we measure token latency (single-stream) and end-to-end (includes network + prefix cache). In Redwood Optimize the recommendations are tuned to keep 95th pct token latency within your SLO. For example on a 13B llama-family model we saw median token latency ~18ms FP16, ~12ms INT8, FP8 sits around 14-15ms depending on kernel.
01:40 Amir Patel: those numbers assume what hardware?
01:43 Priya Shah: A100/80GB equiv; our Dedicated test used 1x A100 vectored with our kernel set. We'll send the raw sheet.
01:51 Jordan Lee: also worth noting the Optimize UI shows quality vs latency curves and suggests quant profile per route — you can pin a profile per model+route.
02:05 Marco Ruiz: ok show us the UI?
02:10 Priya Shah: sure, sharing screen now — (UI commentary) here is Optimize, this route is chat-completions-prod, we have traffic shape, token distribution. You can see recommended quant profiles: stable-int8, conservative-fp8, mixed-int8-fp8 for long-contexts.
02:35 Marco Ruiz: mixed profile? explain that.
02:38 Priya Shah: mixed means we use INT8 for the forward pass on most layers but promote certain sensitive layers (first and last N layers or attention layers) to FP8 to recover quality. It's a good midpoint for latency and quality.
02:52 Sophie Chen: uh-huh, that sounds like something our infra team would like — less memory but also less regres-sion.
03:01 Priya Shah: exact. Also Optimize suggests per-prompt eval sets — we run A/B evals with your prompts to estimate quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim scores or human evals). Here are sample deltas we saw: on a 7B model INT8 had avg embedding-sim drop ~0.012 compared to FP16, FP8 was ~0.004. On 13B those drops shrink.
03:30 Marco Ruiz: are those deltas meaningful in production? Some prompts are safety/precision critical.
03:36 Priya Shah: yes for safety-critical we recommend conservative-fp8 or full fp16. For casual chat where typical tolerance is higher, stable-int8 or mixed is usually fine. We can run your evals through our regression harness.
03:50 Amir Patel: what's the recommended approach to pick profiles? We have 3 routes: search-bot (sensitive), casual-assist (high qps, can tolerate) and docs-summarize (long context).
04:02 Priya Shah: in Optimize you'd create route-specific profiles: search-bot -> conservative-fp8 or fp16, casual-assist -> stable-int8, docs-summarize -> mixed-int8-fp8 + KV cache pref to reduce regen. The console will estimate cost savings too.
04:20 Jordan Lee: we should call out cost numbers — in our benchmark INT8 reduced token compute cost roughly 2.6x vs fp16 on similar throughput; FP8 gave ~1.5x cost reduction. So INT8 is biggest win, FP8 is good middle ground.
04:40 Sophie Chen: those cost ratios include the overhead of conversion and potential batching penalties?
04:46 Priya Shah: yes they include kernel overheads. The caveat: INT8 sometimes needs per-channel calibration and extra prewarm for KV cache shapes, so tail latency can be less predictable unless you use Redwood's recommended batching and caching settings that Optimize suggests.
05:05 Marco Ruiz: can you run a regression test with our 2000 prompt set? We have a labeled subset for quality gating.
05:12 Priya Shah: absolutely, we can onboard that set. If you send it we'll run A/B: fp16 vs stable-int8 and fp8 vs fp16 and give statistical tests and sample failure cases.
05:25 Amir Patel: what's the expected turnaround?
05:27 Priya Shah: usually 3-5 business days to run and compile a report for a 2k prompt set on Dedicated. If it's on Hosted with limited access it might be slower.
05:40 Jordan Lee: we'll propose a pilot: Nova gets a Dedicated pool with specific quant profiles applied to two routes for one week. Priya will run the eval harness on your prompt set.
06:00 Sophie Chen: capacity wise what size Dedicated should we request?
06:04 Priya Shah: for the test workload you described (peak 450 qps across routes) we'd recommend 4x A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale burst to 6 for load. For cheaper test you can do a scaled-down synthetic throughput and we extrapolate.
06:22 Marco Ruiz: how do we ensure the pilot doesn't affect our prod keys or data residency?
06:26 Jordan Lee: pilot can be in your VPC (Private) or Redwood Dedicated with strict routing and no data retention. We can sign an NDA for sample data; all telemetry can be kept out if needed.
06:38 Sophie Chen: ok security looks fine. Also curious — how does mixed quantization impact KV cache size?
06:44 Priya Shah: mixed tends to be similar to INT8 for KV footprint because we still store keys/values in smaller dtype for most layers; a few promoted layers add marginal overhead. Optimize shows expected KV memory impact per profile in the Console.
07:00 Amir Patel: any gotchas with beam search or sampling?
07:04 Priya Shah: sampling randomness is unaffected, but very narrow-beam/high-precision tasks sometimes show token selection differences under INT8. That's where we lean FP8 or layer promotions.
07:20 Marco Ruiz: ok can you show us the benchmark CSV?
07:22 Priya Shah: yes, here's a snippet — (reads) model,profile,median_token_ms,95p_token_ms,avg_embedding_sim,cost_ratio
07:33 Priya Shah: 7B,fp16,16,38,0.000,1.0
07:38 Priya Shah: 7B,stable-int8,9,55, -0.012,0.38
07:44 Priya Shah: 7B,fp8-conservative,11,42,-0.004,0.65
07:50 Amir Patel: interesting the 95p on INT8 is 55ms which is higher than fp16 even though median is lower — is that typical?
07:57 Priya Shah: yes that's the tail effect I mentioned: INT8 can have kernel variance on long contexts or cold KV shapes. Our runtime mitigates this with dynamic batching windows and prefix caching; Optimize suggests a hybrid profile or bumping up min capacity to reduce tail.
08:20 Marco Ruiz: can we pin different profiles by prompt type within same route? Some prompts are known to be safety-critical.
08:26 Priya Shah: you can use routing rules in Console: prompt metadata or route tags can pick a different model/profile. For example if the prompt has 'sensitive:true' tag we route to conservative-fp8.
08:38 Sophie Chen: who typically owns the calibration step for INT8? We don't want to add a heavy ops burden.
08:45 Priya Shah: Redwood offers automated calibration in Optimize — we handle the quant calibration and produce a calibrated artifact you can pin. For Dedicated you can opt to run calibration inside your environment if you prefer.
09:00 Marco Ruiz: do you collect user data during calibration?
09:03 Priya Shah: only the prompts you provide for calibration; you can scrub PII before sending. We also support running the calibration in your VPC so nothing leaves your network.
09:14 Amir Patel: ok good.
09:18 Jordan Lee: one other note — for production we recommend a staged rollout: 1) perf test on Dedicated snapshot, 2) run eval harness on labeled prompts, 3) small canary traffic with auto-fallback to fp16 if quality drift exceeds threshold, 4) widen. Optimize and Console support canary and auto-fallback rules.
09:40 Marco Ruiz: what's the metric you use for auto-fallback? embedding-sim delta?
09:44 Priya Shah: it's configurable — teams use embedding-sim with a threshold plus some heuristic on token-level unexpected logits. We also allow human-in-the-loop gating for first N failures.
09:55 Sophie Chen: on the API side, will switching profiles require client changes?
09:59 Jordan Lee: no — it's transparent server-side. The route in the Console maps to a profile and you can change it without client-side changes.
10:08 Marco Ruiz: ok sounds good. Anything on cost modeling?
10:12 Jordan Lee: Optimize includes cost estimates per-profile: projected monthly compute cost, token cost, and bucketed by route. We'll send an export with your expected qps and tokens.
10:22 Amir Patel: what's the licensing for Dedicated pilot? Any additional fees for Optimize features?
10:26 Jordan Lee: pilot is usually covered under our evaluation credits; long-term Dedicated has reserved pricing. Optimize is included but advanced eval retention or premium support are add-ons. We'll send pricing in the follow-up.
10:40 Marco Ruiz: great, I'm convinced we should run the 1-week pilot on Dedicated.
10:44 Sophie Chen: I have one last infra question — if we later switch some routes to on-prem Private, does the quant profile artifact move with the model?
10:52 Priya Shah: yes, the quant artifacts and runtime kernels are compatible; for Private we ship the calibration artifact and runtime libs or we can compile in your environment. There might be slight kernel/perf variance depending on GPU and driver.
11:05 Marco Ruiz: thanks, that was super helpful.
11:08 Jordan Lee: ok quick recap of actions and timeline — Marco to share prompt set by Friday, Jordan to send benchmarks and pricing, Priya to provision Dedicated pilot and run evals, follow-up meeting next Thursday.
11:22 Amir Patel: sounds good.
11:26 (end)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions present, speaker labels mostly correct but sometimes generic. References: shared benchmark sheet (link: drive.redwood/example-benchmarks.csv), pilot config doc (link: redwood.com/pilots/nova-config).
